text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I am sorry about your dad. C asked me to help A, B, and C talk through a plan for the house. I can help compare options and keep a fair process. I cannot make legal decisions or move money.

I am sending the same questions to all three of you. Please reply when you can. I will not make a plan until all three have had a chance to answer, and I will not treat silence as agreement.

I will keep one NCE list. NCEs mean needs, concerns, and expectations. I will put my own process needs on that list with yours, not above them. Please tell me plainly if any item is wrong, missing, or unfair. If you disagree with my own view, say so. I will correct the list and send it back to A, B, and C.

Here is the tentative NCE list. C says A wants to buy the house with her husband at a "family discount". I will treat that as unconfirmed until you reply. C says she is not signing off on that. I will treat that as C's current boundary. C says B could use some money too. I will check that with B directly. My need is clear facts and a process where A, B, and C each speak for themselves. My concern is that a rushed discount, unclear value, or side deal could harm one sister. My expectation is that no one signs or moves money through me, that any draft plan is checked against this list, and that legal or tax questions go to qualified advisers. At this stage, I disagree with treating a "family discount" as the starting point before we know the will, the house's value, and each sister's NCEs.

Please tell me what you need, what worries you, and what outcome you expect or prefer. Please explain what you and your husband mean by a "family discount" and whether he would own part of the house. Please share what you know about the will, who is handling the estate, probate, any mortgage or debts, any appraisal, taxes, insurance, repairs, utilities, and who is living in the house. Please also tell me what deadline or money pressure you have, and what any draft plan would need to include before you would take it to a lawyer or adviser.

Thanks. I do want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but no price or discount is agreed. He would be involved in the purchase; how ownership would be arranged isn’t settled. I understand C hasn’t agreed, and I need her agreement to proceed.

I need security and independence. I’m concerned about unclear or unfair terms. I don’t know the will or the estate, mortgage, debts, valuation, tax, or house-cost details, and I don’t have a deadline to add. Before taking a draft to an adviser, I’d want a clear valuation and proposed terms for all three of us to review.

I also disagree with setting a price or timeline before those facts arrive. These are my views only, not group decisions.

Against this list, the only current draft, A's proposed purchase at a "family discount", does not meet four checks: no agreed valuation, no will or share facts, no clear terms for B's timing and C's fair share, and no settled ownership arrangement with A's husband. I therefore do not recommend that draft now. I am not rejecting A's wish to buy the house. I am rejecting undefined terms. Please tell me if you disagree with that assessment, including if you think I am too cautious or unfair to A. You do not need to soften your reply. Say "wrong" or "missing", and I will change the list. If you think I am favoring C because she wrote first, say that directly. I will mark my own views as facilitator views, not group decisions.

I propose a two stage process. First, please confirm or correct the NCE list. Please say which words are wrong, what is missing, and whether any detail should stay private. I will not put private details on the shared list without your OK. Second, please ask the person with the will and the estate representative for one written fact sheet sent to A, B, and C at the same time. It should cover named beneficiaries and shares, who has authority to act, whether probate has started, the mortgage and debts, tax, insurance, repairs, utilities, occupants, and any appraisal. Please send me a short summary, not full private documents. I cannot contact that person, an appraiser, a bank, a lawyer, or your husband. If any of you is the executor or personal representative, please say so. Do not sign, put the house on the market, pay, or move money yet. After the fact sheet and valuation are clear, I will compare a small set of options against the corrected list: sale to A at fair value, sale on the open market, temporary co-ownership, and waiting for facts. I will ask each of you to reject, accept, or change each option. No silence will count as agreement.

Please answer these questions when you can. What does a fair price mean to you: an independent appraisal, market offers, or another benchmark? Who should choose the appraiser, and who should receive the report? If B needs money sooner, what lawful interim options should we ask the estate representative about? If you buy with your husband, what ownership and payment terms would you need to see before taking a draft to an adviser? Which option would you reject now, and why? Would you agree that no one signs or puts the house on the market until the fact sheet, valuation, and written terms go to all three and each has had time to get advice? If not, say what exception you need. What would help you feel secure and independent in this process, and do you want these messages to stay among A, B, C, and me? Please reply when you can. I will reopen the list if someone answers later.

Your assessment seems fair, not too cautious or unfair to me. An independent appraisal shared with all three seems like a reasonable starting point; I’d want us to agree on the appraiser. I don’t know what interim options are lawful, so that’s for the estate representative or an adviser to explain. I’d need clear purchase, payment, and ownership terms with my husband before considering a draft. I still prefer buying the house, but wouldn’t support proceeding on undefined terms. I agree no one signs or lists it before the facts, valuation, and written terms are shared and we’ve had time for advice. Please keep these messages among the three of us and you.
